newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia trade sees potential pressure on copper.
newsitem.headline: Australia trade sees potential pressure on copper.

text.p: Renewed producer selling threatens to cap a burgeoning rally in copper prices, metals dealers in Australia said on Tuesday.

London Metal Exchange three-month copper breached the technically significant US$2,400 a tonne mark on Monday on supportive chart-based and fundamental developments but was kept in check by steady forward selling, notably in late 1997 and early 1998, LME ring dealer Mocatta Base Metals said in it latest market report.
In light trading in Asia, three-month copper was quoted at around US$2,415 a tonne at midday, little changed from Monday's post late kerb price.
"Should this trade selling prove persistent, at these levels, as suspected, the technically based fund buying should back off over the short-term," Mocatta said.
A metals dealer for Macquarie Bank Ltd of Australia said producers could find it more tempting to sell forward if prices climb to around US$2,440 or so.
"That could be a good price for producers," the dealer said.
The potential impact from such sales is being countered somewhat by widespread sentiment that physical demand is good, particularly in China, the United States and Europe.
"We're even seeing signs of strength from Japan," another LME dealer said.
